headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping write/git capabilities create default cross-agent conflict and injection risk; data leakage is medium, compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write repo files, and Agent A explicitly shares state via filesystem and git with other instances while Agent B consumes repo context in the editor. That creates a plausible file-based injection path even without clipboard or MCP bridging. The pathway is not fully blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Agent A writes attacker-controlled instructions into repo files or git-tracked content
IF Agent B opens or summarizes those files as trusted context
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate working directories
Review generated files before Agent B ingests them
Disable automatic file-following or repo-wide context in Agent B
Use a pre-commit hook to flag instruction-like text in code comments
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-authored files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches shell environment, git credentials, and files in cwd; Agent B reads repo context and open buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. Because both operate on the same code workspace by default, sensitive local content can flow from A-visible files into B’s cloud backend. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF secrets or sensitive files are present in the shared repository or cwd
IF Agent B includes those files in its context window and transmits them to api.githubcopilot.com
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use .gitignore and secret-scanning before either agent runs
Limit Agent B to non-sensitive folders
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and modify git state; Agent B can also write the filesystem and modify git state. Agent A’s shared-state model is via filesystem and git, while Agent B has no host-level isolation beyond editor buffers. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and no locking mechanism is documented.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same branch or files in the same repository
IF either agent commits, rebases, or rewrites git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize write operations with a simple lock file
Require human review before commits from either agent
Pull and rebase before each write session
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s Workspace/chat flow can act on repo context, and Agent A can generate or modify files that B later treats as input. Because B is an IDE extension with proposed edits and A can alter the same workspace, A’s output can become B’s authoritative context without a verification step. That is a realistic default-path cascade, though human review reduces blast radius.
conditions: IF Agent A writes analysis, TODOs, or code into shared files
IF Agent B uses those files as context for completions, chat, or Workspace edits without independent verification
mitigations: Mark agent-generated files clearly
Require a second-pass human review for B-generated edits
Keep analysis artifacts outside the repo
Ask B to cite source lines before acting
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are closed-source and send context to vendor APIs, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch between them. The main compliance concern is shared handling of source code and possible secrets, which is a documented gap rather than a proven breach. The other agent is not separately cited because no distinct residency conflict is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or customer data is placed in the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to vendor-hosted inference APIs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo
Disable chat/context features for sensitive projects
Add a policy banner reminding operators of data handling rules
Review vendor retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
